phrases.arabic: عَاوِد عَيَّط لِيَا مِن بَعْد شْوِيَة

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: Hello?

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.english: Hello, Salma? It's Samir.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: آه سمير، مرحبا. مزيان بلي عيطتي ليا
dialogue.transliteration: aah Samir, mar7ba. mzyaan bli 3ayyaTti liya
dialogue.english: Oh Samir, hi. Good that you called.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.english: What's new?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: All good, thank God. And you?

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله. عيطت ليك قبيلة، الخط كان مشغول
dialogue.transliteration: l7amdulilah. 3ayyaTt lik qbila, l-khatt kaan mashghool
dialogue.english: Fine, thank God. I called you a bit ago, the line was busy.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: سمح ليا، ما قدرتش نجاوبك قبيلة
dialogue.transliteration: sma7 liya, ma qdertsh njaawbek qbila
dialogue.english: Sorry, I couldn't answer you a bit ago.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.arabic: ما عليك. الخط تقطع ليا حتى أنا
dialogue.english: Never mind. The call got cut off on me too.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: There's no signal here at home.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.arabic: والصولد سالا ليا، والبطارية حتى هي سالات
dialogue.transliteration: w-s-solde sala liya, w l-baTTaariyya 7ta hiya saalat
dialogue.english: And my credit ran out, and my battery died too.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: عَاوِد عَيَّط لِيَا مِن بَعْد شْوِيَة
dialogue.english: Call me back in a bit.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.arabic: واخا، غادي نعيط ليك من بعد. بسلامة
dialogue.transliteration: waakha, ghadi n3ayyaT lik mn ba3d. bslaama
dialogue.english: OK, I'll call you later. Bye.

pair.english: I called you a bit ago.

pair.arabic: عَاوِد عَيَّط لِيَا مِن بَعْد شْوِيَة
pair.english: Call me back in a bit.

lessons.culture: Moroccans usually answer with "ألو" and then ask "شكون معايا؟", and often open with "السلام عليكم" when the caller is older or unknown. Phone credit is topped up in small amounts, so "سالا ليا الصولد" is a very common reason a call stops, and calls end with "بسلامة".

exercises.prompt: You pick up the phone and hear: "ألو؟". Answer naturally, asking who is calling.

too_formal.item: السلام عليكم، من المتصل من فضلك؟
too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "ألو، شكون معايا؟".

exercises.tip: "شكون معايا؟" literally asks who is with me, and is the everyday way to ask who is calling.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks you on the phone: "أش خبارك؟". Say all is well, thank God.

too_formal.item: الأمور على ما يرام، ولله الحمد
too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "الحمد لله، لا باس".

exercises.tip: "لا باس" is the standard Moroccan answer, usually with "الحمد لله".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "ما قدرتش _____ قبيلة." Meaning: I couldn't answer you a bit ago.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "نجاوبك".

exercises.tip: "جاوب" is the everyday verb for answering someone.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "_____ ليا الخط وأنا كنهضر معاك." Meaning: The call got cut off on me while I was talking to you.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "تقطع ليا الخط".

exercises.tip: "كنهضر" means I'm talking; "تقطع ليا الخط" describes a dropped call.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Moroccan Arabic: "My battery died."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "البطارية سالات ليا".

exercises.tip: "سالا" covers running out of almost anything: credit, battery, money.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "There's no signal here."

too_formal.item: لا توجد تغطية في هذا المكان
too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "ما كاينش الريزو هنا".

exercises.tip: "الريزو" (from French réseau) is the everyday word for network signal; "ما كاينش" means there is none.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "My credit ran out"?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "سالا ليا الصولد".

exercises.tip: "الصولد" is prepaid phone credit; "الكريدي" is also heard.

exercises.prompt: Which is the natural way to answer an incoming call?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "ألو؟".

exercises.tip: A short "ألو؟" opens the call, then you ask who it is.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "Call me back in a bit."
exercises.answer: عَاوِد عَيَّط لِيَا مِن بَعْد شْوِيَة
accepted: عَاوِد عَيَّط لِيَا مِن بَعْد شْوِيَة

too_formal.item: هل يمكنك معاودة الاتصال بي بعد قليل؟
too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "عاود عيط ليا من بعد شوية".

exercises.tip: "عاود" before a verb means do it again; "من بعد" means later.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "The line was busy."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "الخط كان مشغول".

exercises.tip: "مشغول" is used for a busy line just as it is for a busy person.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.english: Hello Salma, where should we meet today?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: Let's meet at the cafe.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.english: Good. What time suits you?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: Is 7 o'clock good?

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.english: OK. Where exactly?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: عند مسجد الحسن التاني. نلقاك تما
dialogue.english: At the Hassan II Mosque. I'll meet you there.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.arabic: عارف فين هي البلاصة بالضبط. ما تعطلش
dialogue.transliteration: 3aaref feen hiya l-blaaSa bD-DabT. ma t3attelsh
dialogue.english: I know exactly where the place is. Don't be late.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: I'll be there before you, don't worry.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.english: If you're late, call me.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: واخا. شنو رأيك، نمشيو مع بعضنا؟
dialogue.transliteration: waakha. shnu ra2yek, nemshiw m3a b3Dna?
dialogue.english: OK. What do you think, shall we go together?

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.english: Good idea. We'll meet at seven.

lessons.culture: Friends usually settle on a cafe, or on a well-known landmark or square. "ما تعطلش" is said even between close friends, and "إن شاء الله" often follows a time to promise it.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks you: "فين نتلاقاو؟". Suggest meeting at the cafe.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "خلينا نتلاقاو فالكافي".

exercises.tip: "خلينا" plus a verb is the everyday way to suggest doing something together.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: "ما تعطلش!". Tell them you will arrive before them.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "غادي نوصل قبلك".

exercises.tip: "غادي" before a verb marks the future.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "شمن _____ كتناسبك؟" Meaning: What time suits you?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "شمن ساعة كتناسبك؟".

exercises.tip: "شمن ساعة" literally asks which hour.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "نلقاك _____." Meaning: I'll meet you there.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "نلقاك تما".

exercises.tip: "تما" means there; "هنا" is here.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Moroccan Arabic: "Don't be late."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "ما تعطلش".

exercises.tip: "ما ... ش" wraps a verb to make a negative.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Where exactly?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "فين بالضبط؟".

exercises.tip: "فين" is where in Moroccan Arabic.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks "Where should we meet?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "فين نتلاقاو؟".

exercises.tip: "نتلاقاو" is we meet.

exercises.prompt: You want to suggest going together. Which sentence do you say?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "شنو رأيك، نمشيو مع بعضنا؟".

exercises.tip: "مع بعضنا" means together.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "Is 7 o'clock good?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "واش السبعة مزيانة؟".

exercises.tip: "واش" at the start turns a sentence into a yes/no question.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "If you're late, call me."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "إلا تعطلتي، عيط ليا".

exercises.tip: "إلا" opens an if clause.

phrases.arabic: خْلِينَا نْلَقَاو نْهَار كْيَنَاسْبْنَا حْنَا الْجُوج

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.english: Hello Salma, I want to change the appointment.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: Why? What happened?

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.arabic: وقعات ليا شي حاجة، ما نقدرش نجي اليوم
dialogue.transliteration: waq3at liya shi 7aaja, ma nqdersh nji lyoum
dialogue.english: Something came up for me, I can't come today.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: ما كاين مشكل. واش نأجلوه لغدا؟
dialogue.transliteration: ma kayn mushkil. wash n2ajjluh l-ghedda?
dialogue.english: No problem. Can we postpone to tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.english: Can we meet in the afternoon instead of the morning?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: OK. Is the place still the same place?

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.arabic: إيه، هو هو. سمح ليا، بدلت الموعد فجأة
dialogue.transliteration: iyyeh, huwa huwa. sma7 liya, beddelt l-maw3id fej2a
dialogue.english: Yes, the same. Sorry, I changed the appointment suddenly.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: Never mind, these things happen.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.arabic: ولا نلقاك نهار الجمعة عوض الخميس؟
dialogue.english: Or I'll meet you Friday instead of Thursday?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: الجمعة مزيان، غير من بعد الصلاة
dialogue.transliteration: j-jem3a mzyaan, ghir mn ba3d S-Salaa
dialogue.english: Friday is good, just after the prayer.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.english: Thanks a lot, God keep you.

pair.english: I want to change the appointment.

response.english: No problem, we'll postpone to tomorrow.

pair.english: Is the place still the same?

lessons.culture: Postponing is accepted as long as you say so early and apologise with "سمح ليا"; a vague "وقعات ليا شي حاجة" is a full reason and nobody asks for more. Friday midday is the prayer and the family couscous lunch, so plans on that day are set for after the prayer.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "واش نتلاقاو اليوم؟". You cannot; say something came up for you.
exercises.answer: ما نقدرش نجي اليوم، وقعات ليا شي حاجة
accepted: ما نقدرش نجي اليوم، وقعات ليا شي حاجة
ma nqdersh nji lyoum, waq3at liya shi 7aaja

too_formal.item: لا أستطيع الحضور اليوم لأن ظرفا طرأ
too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "ما نقدرش نجي اليوم، وقعات ليا شي حاجة".

exercises.tip: "شي حاجة" is a polite, unspecific reason.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: "سمح ليا على التبديل". Tell them it is no problem.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "ما كاين مشكل".

exercises.tip: "ما عليك" and "ما كاين مشكل" both wave the apology away.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "بغيت _____ الموعد." Meaning: I want to change the appointment.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "بغيت نبدل الموعد".

exercises.tip: "بغيت" plus a verb without "أن" means I want to.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "نتلاقاو العشية _____ الصباح." Meaning: We meet in the afternoon instead of the morning.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "نتلاقاو العشية عوض الصباح".

exercises.tip: "عوض" means instead of.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Moroccan Arabic: "Can we postpone to tomorrow?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "واش نأجلوه لغدا؟".

exercises.tip: "غدا" is tomorrow, said with the "ل" as "لغدا".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'll meet you Friday instead of Thursday."

too_formal.item: سأقابلك يوم الجمعة بدلا من الخميس
too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "نلقاك نهار الجمعة عوض الخميس".

exercises.tip: "نهار" is day, used before the name of a weekday.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Can we cancel the appointment?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "واش نلغيو الموعد؟".

exercises.tip: "لغى" is the everyday verb for cancel.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence apologises for a sudden change?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "سمح ليا، بدلت الموعد فجأة".

exercises.tip: "سمح ليا" is the everyday sorry.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "Let's find a day that suits us both."
exercises.answer: خْلِينَا نْلَقَاو نْهَار كْيَنَاسْبْنَا حْنَا الْجُوج
accepted: خْلِينَا نْلَقَاو نْهَار كْيَنَاسْبْنَا حْنَا الْجُوج
خلينا نلقاو نهار مزيان ليا وليك
خلينا نلقاو نهار مزيان لينا جوج

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "خلينا نلقاو نهار كيناسبنا حنا الجوج".

exercises.tip: "الجوج" means both, so "حنا الجوج" is both of us.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "Is the place still the same place?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "واش المكان هو هو؟".

exercises.tip: "هو هو" said twice means the very same.

phrases.arabic: مَا عْرَفْتِش بَالضَّبْط، مِن بَعْد شْوِيَة
مَزْيَان بْلِي مَا ضِيعْتِش لِيك الْوَقْت
phrases.transliteration: mzyaan bli ma DayyaTsh lik l-weqt

phrases.arabic: غَادِي نُوصَل لِيه الْخَبَر غِير يِدْخُل

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.english: Hello?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: ألو، السلام عليكم. واش سمير كاين؟
dialogue.english: Hello, peace be upon you. Is Samir there?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: وعليكم السلام. لا، ما كاينش دابا
dialogue.english: And peace on you. No, he's not here right now.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: When will he be back?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: مَا عْرَفْتِش بَالضَّبْط، مِن بَعْد شْوِيَة
dialogue.english: I don't know exactly, in a bit.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: Can you take a message for me?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.english: Sure, go ahead.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: Tell him to call me.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.english: Does he have your number?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: إيه، ولكن قول ليه بلي عيطت

dialogue.speaker: Youssef

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: Thanks a lot. Bye.

response.english: No, he's not here right now.

response.arabic: مَا عْرَفْتِش بَالضَّبْط، مِن بَعْد شْوِيَة
response.english: I don't know exactly, in a bit.

pair.english: Can you take a message for me?

lessons.culture: A family member often picks up the home phone, so the caller greets first with "السلام عليكم" and only then asks for the person. Messages are passed on by word of mouth with "قول ليه", and thanks are often followed by a short prayer such as "الله يخليك".

exercises.prompt: Someone answers your call: "ألو؟". Ask if Samir is there.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "ألو، واش سمير كاين؟".

exercises.tip: "كاين" means is present, is there.

exercises.prompt: You are asked: "إمتا غادي يرجع؟". Say you don't know exactly, in a bit.
exercises.answer: مَا عْرَفْتِش بَالضَّبْط، مِن بَعْد شْوِيَة
accepted: مَا عْرَفْتِش بَالضَّبْط، مِن بَعْد شْوِيَة

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "ما عرفتش بالضبط، من بعد شوية".

exercises.tip: "ما عرفتش" is the everyday I don't know.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "قول ليه _____ ليا." Meaning: Tell him to call me.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "قول ليه يعيط ليا".

exercises.tip: "عيط ل" is the everyday verb for phone someone.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "غير يوصل _____." Meaning: I'll tell him as soon as he arrives.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "غير يوصل نقول ليه".

exercises.tip: "غير" before a verb means as soon as.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Moroccan Arabic: "Can you take a message for me?"
accepted: واش تقدر توصل ليه شي رسالة

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "واش تقدر توصل ليه رسالة؟".

exercises.tip: "واش تقدر" is the everyday way to ask can you.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Do you have my number?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "واش عندك نيميرو ديالي؟".

exercises.tip: "ديالي" is mine, placed after the noun.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "When will he be back?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "إمتا غادي يرجع؟".

exercises.tip: "إمتا" is when.

exercises.prompt: Which do you say to thank someone warmly?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "شكرا بزاف".

exercises.tip: "بزاف" means a lot.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "Let him know I called."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "قول ليه بلي عيطت".

exercises.tip: "بلي" means that, before a whole sentence.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "He's not here right now."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic, but everyday Moroccan speech says "ما كاينش دابا".

exercises.tip: "دابا" is now.

challenge.title: A Phone Call to Rearrange Plans
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a phone conversation of at least 10 lines. It must include answering the phone, proposing a place and a time to meet, changing that plan for a real reason, agreeing on a new time or place, and, if the person you called is not free, leaving a message for someone else to pass on.
required_elements: Asking or stating who is calling, using شكون معايا or معاك + name.
A suggestion of where to meet, using خلينا نتلاقاو or a similar phrase.
A question about time, using شمن ساعة كتناسبك or واش السبعة مزيانة.
A reason for changing the plan, using وقعات ليا شي حاجة or a similar phrase.
A request to postpone or change, using واش نأجلوه or بغيت نبدل الموعد.
An apology for the change, using سمح ليا or a similar phrase.
A reassurance in response, using ما كاين مشكل or ما عليك.
A closing thank-you, using شكرا بزاف or الله يخليك.
At least one exchange about leaving or taking a message, using رسالة or قول ليه.

dialogue.arabic: ألو سلمى، وقعات ليا شي حاجة، ما نقدرش نجي غدا. واش نأجلوه لنهار الجمعة؟
dialogue.transliteration: alo Salma, waq3at liya shi 7aaja, ma nqdersh nji ghedda. wash n2ajjluh l-nhaar j-jem3a?
dialogue.english: Hello Salma, something came up, I can't come tomorrow. Can we postpone to Friday?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: ما كاين مشكل. الجمعة مزيان، غير من بعد الصلاة
dialogue.transliteration: ma kayn mushkil. j-jem3a mzyaan, ghir mn ba3d S-Salaa
dialogue.english: No problem. Friday is good, just after the prayer.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.arabic: سمح ليا على التبديل. إلا ما جاوبتش، خلي رسالة عند خويا
dialogue.transliteration: sma7 liya 3la t-tebdeel. ila ma jaawebtsh, khelli risaala 3and khuya
dialogue.english: Sorry for the change. If I don't answer, leave a message with my brother.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: OK, I'll tell him I called.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.english: Thanks a lot, God keep you.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: Bye.
